knowledgeMeta.content:
# Black Hole Accretion

Accretion converts gravitational energy into radiation and is the main way black
holes are observed. The Eddington limit, the ISCO, and radiative efficiency set
the luminosity and growth rate.

## Eddington limit and efficiency

Balancing radiation pressure against gravity on ionized hydrogen gives

$$L_{\rm Edd} = \frac{4\pi GMm_pc}{\sigma_T}\approx1.26\times10^{38}\frac{M}{M_\odot}\ \mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}.$$

With radiative efficiency $\epsilon$, up to $\sim5.7\%$ of rest mass is radiated
at the Schwarzschild ISCO, and up to $\sim42\%$ for prograde orbits at the
extremal [[Kerr Metric]] ISCO. The mass growth rate is
$\dot M=(1-\epsilon)L/(\epsilon c^2)$; see
[[Early Supermassive Black Hole Growth]].

## Observational tracers

For stellar-mass black holes, the BlackCAT catalog compiles black-hole X-ray
binaries, and the broad Fe K$\alpha$ line profile and continuum fitting yield
spins (from $a_*\approx0$ in A0620-00 to $a_*\approx0.998$ in GRS 1915+105). For
supermassive black holes, AGN reverberation mapping uses broad-line response
delays and line velocities to estimate masses; the local compilation in this
workspace contains 86 nearby AGN and is method-comparison context, not an
early-Universe sample. Quasi-periodic oscillations may trace orbital motion at
the ISCO. Accretion also powers the electromagnetic output of the events in
[[Gravitational-Wave Catalogs]] and the emission around [[White Holes]] in
speculative models.

See also: [[Early Supermassive Black Hole Growth]], [[Schwarzschild Metric]], [[Kerr Metric]], [[Hawking Radiation]], [[Gravitational-Wave Catalogs]]

Categories: Black Holes, Observations & Catalogs

nodes.name: Christoffel Symbols
nodes.summary: Christoffel symbols encode the affine connection of a spacetime and are the first step in computing geodesics, curvature, and tidal forces.

knowledgeMeta.content:
# Christoffel Symbols

Christoffel symbols encode the affine connection of a spacetime and are the
first step in computing geodesics, curvature, and tidal forces.

## Definition

Given a metric $g_{\mu\nu}$ with inverse $g^{\mu\nu}$,

$$\Gamma^\lambda_{\mu\nu} = \frac12 g^{\lambda\sigma}\left(\partial_\mu g_{\nu\sigma}+\partial_\nu g_{\mu\sigma}-\partial_\sigma g_{\mu\nu}\right).$$

They are symmetric in the lower indices, $\Gamma^\lambda_{\mu\nu}=\Gamma^\lambda_{\nu\mu}$.

## Schwarzschild

For [[Schwarzschild Metric]], with $A=e^{2\alpha}$ and $B=e^{2\beta}$, the
non-vanishing components include

$$\Gamma^t_{\ tr}=\alpha', \quad \Gamma^r_{\ tt}=\alpha'\frac{A}{B}, \quad
\Gamma^r_{\ rr}=\beta', \quad \Gamma^r_{\ \theta\theta}=-\frac{r}{B}, \quad
\Gamma^\theta_{\ r\theta}=\frac1r, \quad \Gamma^\phi_{\ r\phi}=\frac1r.$$

These are the building blocks for the vacuum field equations and for the tidal
acceleration.

## Kerr

For [[Kerr Metric]] the determinant is $\det g=-\rho^4\sin^2\theta$ and the
inverse metric has $g^{rr}=\Delta/\rho^2$, $g^{\theta\theta}=1/\rho^2$,
$g^{tt}=-[(r^2+a^2)^2-a^2\Delta\sin^2\theta]/(\rho^2\Delta)$, and
$g^{t\phi}=-2Mra/(\rho^2\Delta)$. There are 20 independent (48 with symmetry)
non-zero components. For example,

$$\Gamma^r_{\ tt} = \frac{M(r^2-a^2\cos^2\theta)\Delta}{\rho^6}, \qquad
\Gamma^r_{\theta\theta}=-\frac{r\Delta}{\rho^2}, \qquad
\Gamma^\theta_{\ r\theta}=\frac{r}{\rho^2}.$$

In the Schwarzschild limit $a\to0$ these reduce to the expressions above, and as
$M,a\to0$ they reduce to the spherical-coordinate symbols of flat space. The
symbols feed directly into [[Geodesic Equations]] and the
[[Raychaudhuri Equation]].

See also: [[Kerr Metric]], [[Schwarzschild Metric]], [[Geodesic Equations]], [[Raychaudhuri Equation]]

Categories: Gravity & Spacetime

knowledgeMeta.content:
# Early Supermassive Black Hole Growth

How supermassive black holes reached billions of solar masses within the first
billion years is an open problem. Observations of high-redshift quasars and
AGN set the growth budget; accretion physics supplies the clock.

## The growth equation

The Eddington luminosity for fully ionized hydrogen is
$L_{\rm Edd}=4\pi GMm_pc/\sigma_T\approx1.26\times10^{38}(M/M_\odot)$ erg/s.
With radiative efficiency $\epsilon$, Eddington ratio
$\lambda=L/L_{\rm Edd}$, and duty fraction $f_{\rm duty}$, the retained mass
grows as

$$\frac{dM}{dt}=\frac{1-\epsilon}{\epsilon}f_{\rm duty}\lambda\frac{4\pi Gm_p}{\sigma_T c}M,$$

so $M=M_0\exp[(t-t_0)/t_{\rm ef}]$ with e-folding time

$$t_{\rm ef}=\frac{\epsilon}{1-\epsilon}\frac{\sigma_T c}{4\pi Gm_p}\frac{1}{f_{\rm duty}\lambda}.$$

For $\epsilon=0.1$ and continuous Eddington-limited accretion, $t_{\rm ef}\approx50$ Myr.

## Observational ledger

High-redshift systems include the quasar J0313$-$1806 at $z=7.64$
($M_{\rm BH}=(1.6\pm0.4)\times10^9M_\odot$), CEERS_1019 at $z=8.68$
($\log_{10}M_{\rm BH}=6.95\pm0.37$), GN-z11 at $z=10.6$, and the X-ray source
UHZ1 at $z\approx10.1$. Abell 2744-QSO1 at $z=7.04$ is notable for resolved gas
kinematics. Each measurement has distinct method systematics; none establishes
a unique seed channel.

## Seed channels

Population III remnants, direct-collapse heavy seeds, nuclear-cluster pathways,
and primordial black holes remain viable. Earlier formation, more massive
seeds, higher duty cycles, or mergers can compensate for one another, so a
final mass and epoch constrain the integrated budget, not the seed alone. The
accretion physics connects to [[Black Hole Accretion]] and the remnant masses
to [[Gravitational Wave Analysis]]; primordial seeds connect to [[Quantum Gravity]].

See also: [[Black Hole Accretion]], [[Gravitational Wave Analysis]], [[Quantum Gravity]]

Categories: Observations & Catalogs

knowledgeMeta.content:
# Fisher Information Matrix

The Fisher information matrix (FIM) estimates parameter uncertainties for
gravitational-wave signals. In the high signal-to-noise limit the posterior is
approximately Gaussian with covariance equal to the inverse Fisher matrix.

## Inner product and definition

Detector noise is described by a one-sided power spectral density $S_n(f)$, and
the noise-weighted inner product is

$$(a|b) = 4\Re\int_{f_{\min}}^{f_{\max}}\frac{\tilde a(f)\tilde b^*(f)}{S_n(f)}\,df.$$

The signal-to-noise ratio is $\rho=\sqrt{(h|h)}$. For a signal
$h(\theta)$ with parameters $\theta^i$, the Fisher matrix is

$$\Gamma_{ij} = \left(\frac{\partial h}{\partial\theta^i}\middle|\frac{\partial h}{\partial\theta^j}\right),
\qquad \Sigma^{ij}=(\Gamma^{-1})^{ij},$$

with 1-$\sigma$ errors $\sigma_{\theta^i}=\sqrt{\Sigma^{ii}}$.

## Waveform derivatives and degeneracies

Writing $\tilde h=Ae^{i\Psi}$, the derivative splits into amplitude and phase
parts,

$$\frac{\partial\tilde h}{\partial\theta^i}=\left(\frac{\partial\ln A}{\partial\theta^i}+i\frac{\partial\Psi}{\partial\theta^i}\right)\tilde h.$$

The chirp mass dominates the phase, $\partial\Psi/\partial\mathcal M_c\propto f^{-8/3}$,
so it is measured best; the symmetric mass ratio and effective spin enter at
higher post-Newtonian orders and are strongly degenerate
($\rho_{\mathcal M_c\eta}\approx0.9$–$0.99$). Distance and inclination are
degenerate for a single detector but broken by a network. These forecasts feed
[[Gravitational Wave Analysis]] and are applied to the events in
[[Gravitational-Wave Catalogs]]; the underlying waveforms come from
[[Kerr Metric]] ringdown.

See also: [[Gravitational Wave Analysis]], [[Gravitational-Wave Catalogs]], [[Kerr Metric]]

Categories: Methods, Observations & Catalogs

nodes.name: Geodesic Equations
nodes.summary: The motion of test particles and light in a black-hole spacetime is governed by the geodesic equation

knowledgeMeta.content:
# Geodesic Equations

The motion of test particles and light in a black-hole spacetime is governed by
the geodesic equation

$$\frac{d^2 x^\mu}{d\lambda^2} + \Gamma^\mu_{\nu\rho}\frac{dx^\nu}{d\lambda}\frac{dx^\rho}{d\lambda}=0,$$

where $\lambda$ is an affine parameter. For the Schwarzschild and Kerr metrics
this equation is integrable because enough conserved quantities exist.

## Conserved quantities and the effective potential

For [[Schwarzschild Metric]] the Lagrangian
$\mathcal L=\tfrac12 g_{\mu\nu}\dot x^\mu\dot x^\nu$ gives energy
$E=f(r)\dot t$ and angular momentum $L_z=r^2\sin^2\theta\,\dot\phi$. The
normalization condition yields a one-dimensional radial equation with the
effective potential

$$V_{\rm eff}(r) = f(r)\left(\epsilon+\frac{L^2}{r^2}\right), \qquad f(r)=1-\frac{2M}{r},$$

where $\epsilon=-1$ for timelike and $0$ for null geodesics. Circular orbits
satisfy $dV_{\rm eff}/dr=0$, giving $L^2=Mr^2/(r-3M)$; marginal stability gives
the ISCO $r=6M$. The same machinery yields the photon sphere $r=3M$ and the
pericenter advance $\Delta\phi=6\pi M/[a(1-e^2)]$.

## Kerr and the Carter constant

For [[Kerr Metric]] stationarity and axisymmetry give $E$ and $L_z$, while a
hidden symmetry (a rank-2 Killing tensor) provides the Carter constant

$$\mathcal Q = p_\theta^2 + (L_z\csc\theta - aE\sin\theta)^2 + \epsilon a^2\cos^2\theta.$$

The Hamilton–Jacobi equation then separates, giving

$$\rho^4\dot r^2 = R(r), \qquad \rho^4\dot\theta^2 = \Theta(\theta),$$

with quartic radial potential $R(r)$ and polar potential $\Theta(\theta)$.
Mino time $d\lambda=d\tau/\rho^2$ decouples the two motions entirely. Equatorial
ISCO radii are given by the Bardeen formula. These same null geodesics set the
shadow size used in [[Gravitational Wave Analysis]] and catalog
[[Gravitational-Wave Catalogs]] tests.

See also: [[Schwarzschild Metric]], [[Kerr Metric]], [[Christoffel Symbols]], [[Gravitational Wave Analysis]], [[Gravitational-Wave Catalogs]]

Categories: Gravity & Spacetime

knowledgeMeta.content:
# Gravitational Wave Analysis

Gravitational waves from compact binaries are the primary observational window
onto black holes. The waveform has three phases, each carrying different
information about the source.

## Inspiral, merger, ringdown

During inspiral the chirp mass
$\mathcal M=(m_1m_2)^{3/5}/(m_1+m_2)^{1/5}$ sets the frequency evolution,

$$f_{\rm GW}(t)=\frac{1}{8\pi}\left[\frac{5}{256}\frac{1}{\mathcal M^{5/3}}(t_{\rm coal}-t)\right]^{-3/8}.$$

At merger the peak luminosity briefly reaches $L_{\rm peak}\sim c^5/G\approx3.6\times10^{52}$ W.
The remnant settles to [[Kerr Metric]] through quasinormal-mode ringdown,
$\omega_{\rm QNM}\approx(c^3/GM)[1-0.63(1-a_*)^{3/10}]$. The no-hair theorem
predicts the ringdown spectrum is fixed by $M$ and $J$, so measuring multiple
modes tests the Kerr hypothesis. Parameter estimation uses the
[[Fisher Information Matrix]].

## Other messengers

The Event Horizon Telescope imaged the shadows of M87* ($6.5\times10^9M_\odot$,
$\sim42\,\mu$as) and Sgr A* ($4.0\times10^6M_\odot$, $\sim51.8\,\mu$as) at 230 GHz,
consistent with the photon-ring prediction $\theta_{\rm ring}\approx2.6R_s/D$.
X-ray spectroscopy of the broad Fe K$\alpha$ line and continuum fitting measure
spins, and high-frequency QPOs may track orbital motion at the ISCO. The full
detected-event sample is collected in [[Gravitational-Wave Catalogs]], and the
early-Universe growth of supermassive remnants is discussed in
[[Early Supermassive Black Hole Growth]]. Wormhole models predict echoes, a
signature of [[Wormholes]].

See also: [[Fisher Information Matrix]], [[Gravitational-Wave Catalogs]], [[Kerr Metric]], [[Geodesic Equations]], [[Wormholes]]

Categories: Observations & Catalogs

knowledgeMeta.content:
# Gravitational-Wave Catalogs

The LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA collaborations publish compact-binary merger events in the
Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog (GWTC), served through the Gravitational
Wave Open Science Center (GWOSC).

## What the catalog contains

Each event records source-frame component masses $m_1,m_2$, the chirp mass
$\mathcal M_c$, the effective spin $\chi_{\rm eff}$, luminosity distance,
redshift, network matched-filter SNR, and the final (remnant) mass and spin.
The catalog endpoint is a public read-only JSON service; the local workspace
snapshot contains a deduplicated table of 391 events plus a 301-event O4 table.
A catalog event is not a continuously monitored observation, and missing
parameters must not be read as zero.

## The remnant sample

Remnant masses are inferred from the inspiral and ringdown. GW150914, the first
detection, had $m_1=36^{+5}_{-4}M_\odot$, $m_2=29\pm4M_\odot$, a final mass
$M_f=62\pm4M_\odot$, and spin $a_f=0.67^{+0.05}_{-0.07}$, radiating about
$3M_\odot c^2$. GW190521 produced a $\sim142M_\odot$ remnant in the
pair-instability mass gap. The remnant spins cluster at moderate $a_*$, a
constraint on formation channels.

## Using the sample

The events underpin the parameter-estimation forecasts in
[[Fisher Information Matrix]] and the waveform analysis in
[[Gravitational Wave Analysis]]. Remnant mass and spin connect to
[[Kerr Metric]], and the most massive remnants to growth models in
[[Early Supermassive Black Hole Growth]].

See also: [[Gravitational Wave Analysis]], [[Fisher Information Matrix]], [[Kerr Metric]], [[Early Supermassive Black Hole Growth]]

Categories: Observations & Catalogs

knowledgeMeta.content:
# Hawking Radiation

Hawking radiation is the thermal emission predicted for black holes by quantum
field theory on a curved background. It makes black holes behave like black
bodies with a temperature set by their surface gravity.

## Surface gravity and temperature

The surface gravity of a static black hole is
$\kappa=\lim_{r\to r_+}\tfrac{c^2}{2}f'(r)$. For [[Schwarzschild Metric]] this
gives $\kappa=c^4/(4GM)$, and Hawking's calculation yields

$$T_H = \frac{\hbar\kappa}{2\pi k_B c} = \frac{\hbar c^3}{8\pi G M k_B}.$$

A solar-mass hole has $T_H\approx6\times10^{-8}$ K, far colder than the CMB, so
it currently absorbs more than it emits.

## Power, lifetime, and entropy

Neglecting greybody factors, the radiated power and evaporation time are

$$P = \frac{\hbar c^6}{15360\pi G^2 M^2}, \qquad
\tau = \frac{5120\pi G^2 M_0^3}{\hbar c^4}.$$

For a solar mass, $\tau\sim2\times10^{67}$ yr, about $10^{57}$ times the age of
the Universe. The Bekenstein–Hawking entropy is

$$S_{\rm BH} = \frac{k_B c^3 A}{4G\hbar} = \frac{4\pi k_B G M^2}{\hbar c}.$$

## Thermodynamics and the information paradox

The four laws of black-hole mechanics hold with $\kappa$ as temperature and $A$
as entropy; the first law is $dM=(\kappa/8\pi G)dA+\Omega_H dJ+\Phi dQ$ (see
[[Kerr Metric]] and [[Kerr-Newman Metric]]). Because the radiation is thermal,
a fully evaporated hole appears to destroy information, motivating the
information paradox and proposed resolutions such as remnants, correlations
(Page curve), holography, and firewalls. The deep connection to quantum
spacetime is treated in [[Quantum Gravity]], and the time-reversed analog in
[[White Holes]].

See also: [[Schwarzschild Metric]], [[Kerr Metric]], [[Kerr-Newman Metric]], [[Quantum Gravity]], [[White Holes]]

Categories: Black Holes, Quantum Gravity

knowledgeMeta.content:
# Kerr Metric

The Kerr metric is the unique stationary, axisymmetric vacuum solution of
Einstein's equations: a rotating black hole of mass $M$ and angular momentum
$J=acM$. It is the geometry that real astrophysical black holes are expected
to approximate.

## Line element

In Boyer–Lindquist coordinates $(t,r,\theta,\phi)$, with

$$\rho^2 = r^2 + \frac{a^2}{c^2}\cos^2\theta, \qquad
\Delta = r^2 - \frac{2GMr}{c^2} + \frac{a^2}{c^2},$$

the line element is

$$ds^2 = -\left(1-\frac{2GMr}{\rho^2 c^2}\right)c^2 dt^2
-\frac{4GMar\sin^2\theta}{\rho^2 c}\,dt\,d\phi
+\frac{\rho^2}{\Delta}dr^2 + \rho^2 d\theta^2
+\left(r^2+\frac{a^2}{c^2}+\frac{2GMa^2 r\sin^2\theta}{\rho^2 c^4}\right)\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2.$$

The dimensionless spin is $a_* = ac^2/(GM)=Jc/(GM^2)\in[0,1]$.

## Horizons and ergosphere

The horizons are the roots of $\Delta=0$:

$$r_\pm = \frac{GM}{c^2}\left(1\pm\sqrt{1-a_*^2}\right),$$

where $r_+$ is the event horizon and $r_-$ the inner (Cauchy) horizon. For
$a_*>1$ no horizon exists, which cosmic censorship forbids. The ergosphere
lies between $r_+$ and the static limit $r_{\rm erg}(\theta)$, where $g_{tt}=0$:

$$r_{\rm erg}(\theta) = \frac{GM}{c^2}+\sqrt{\left(\frac{GM}{c^2}\right)^2-\frac{a^2}{c^2}\cos^2\theta}.$$

Inside, no observer can remain static; frame dragging forces co-rotation.

## ISCO and energy extraction

The Bardeen–Press–Teukolsky ISCO is

$$r_{\rm ISCO} = \frac{GM}{c^2}\left[3+Z_2\mp\sqrt{(3-Z_1)(3+Z_1+2Z_2)}\right],$$

with $Z_1 = 1+(1-a_*^2)^{1/3}[(1+a_*)^{1/3}+(1-a_*)^{1/3}]$ and
$Z_2=\sqrt{3a_*^2+Z_1^2}$. The upper sign is prograde. For $a_*=0$ this gives
$6GM/c^2$; for $a_*=1$ prograde, $GM/c^2$. Rotational energy can be extracted
through the Penrose process and through superradiance, $\omega < m\Omega_H$
with $\Omega_H = a_*c^3/[2GM(1+\sqrt{1-a_*^2})]$.

See also: [[Schwarzschild Metric]], [[Kerr-Newman Metric]], [[Geodesic Equations]], [[Christoffel Symbols]], [[Hawking Radiation]], [[Raychaudhuri Equation]]

Categories: Black Holes, Gravity & Spacetime

nodes.name: Kerr-Newman Metric
nodes.summary: The Kerr–Newman metric is the most general stationary, axisymmetric, asymptotically flat solution of the Einstein–Maxwell equations: a black hole with mass $M$, spin $a=J/M$, and charge $Q$.

knowledgeMeta.content:
# Kerr-Newman Metric

The Kerr–Newman metric is the most general stationary, axisymmetric,
asymptotically flat solution of the Einstein–Maxwell equations: a black hole
with mass $M$, spin $a=J/M$, and charge $Q$.

## Metric and horizons

In Boyer–Lindquist coordinates,

$$\Delta = r^2 - 2GMr + a^2 + GQ^2, \qquad \Sigma = r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta,$$

and the electromagnetic potential is
$A_\mu dx^\mu = -(GQr/\Sigma)dt + (GQra\sin^2\theta/\Sigma)d\phi$. Horizons
satisfy $\Delta=0$:

$$r_\pm = GM \pm \sqrt{G^2M^2 - a^2 - GQ^2},$$

with extremality $G^2M^2=a^2+GQ^2$ and horizon area $A=4\pi(r_+^2+a^2)$. The
ergosphere boundary is $r_{\rm ergo}(\theta)=GM+\sqrt{G^2M^2-a^2\cos^2\theta-GQ^2}$.

## Thermodynamics and invariants

Surface gravity, temperature, and horizon angular velocity are

$$\kappa = \frac{r_+-r_-}{2(r_+^2+a^2)}, \qquad
T_H = \frac{\kappa}{2\pi}, \qquad
\Omega_H = \frac{a}{r_+^2+a^2}.$$

The first law and Smarr formula are

$$dM = \frac{\kappa}{8\pi G}dA + \Omega_H dJ + \Phi_+ dQ, \qquad
M = 2T_H S + 2\Omega_H J + \Phi_+ Q.$$

The black hole has gyromagnetic ratio $g=2$, like a Dirac particle, and obeys
$G^2M^2 \ge a^2 + GQ^2$ (cosmic censorship).

## Hidden symmetries and mass

Geodesics are integrable because of a rank-2 Killing tensor and the Carter
constant; see [[Geodesic Equations]]. Conserved charges can be computed as ADM,
Komar, or Wald (Noether) surface integrals, all agreeing: $M_{\rm ADM}=M$,
$J_{\rm ADM}=Ma$, $Q_{\rm ADM}=Q$. The Christodoulou–Ruffini mass formula
splits the mass into irreducible, Coulomb, and rotational parts. The uncharged
limit is [[Kerr Metric]]; setting $a=0$ gives [[Reissner-Nordström Metric]].

See also: [[Kerr Metric]], [[Reissner-Nordström Metric]], [[Schwarzschild Metric]], [[Geodesic Equations]], [[Black Hole Accretion]]

Categories: Black Holes, Gravity & Spacetime

nodes.name: Quantum Gravity
nodes.summary: Quantum gravity is the attempt to describe spacetime and gravity quantum mechanically. No complete theory is experimentally confirmed, but the motivations and candidate frameworks are well mapped.

knowledgeMeta.content:
# Quantum Gravity

Quantum gravity is the attempt to describe spacetime and gravity quantum
mechanically. No complete theory is experimentally confirmed, but the
motivations and candidate frameworks are well mapped.

## Why it is needed

General relativity makes geometry dynamical, while quantum field theory assumes
a fixed background. Matter QFT on a curved background is predictive and gives
Hawking radiation ([[Hawking Radiation]]), but at the Planck scale or during
black-hole evaporation a quantum description of spacetime itself is required.

## Planck scales

Combining $G$, $\hbar$, and $c$ gives

$$\ell_P=\sqrt{\frac{\hbar G}{c^3}}, \quad t_P=\sqrt{\frac{\hbar G}{c^5}}, \quad
m_P=\sqrt{\frac{\hbar c}{G}}, \quad T_P=\frac{m_Pc^2}{k_B}.$$

The Schwarzschild radius and the Compton wavelength cross near $m\approx m_P/\sqrt2$,
which is the order-of-magnitude motivation for the Planck scale.

## Approaches

Gravitational effective field theory is predictive order by order below its
cutoff but does not specify a UV completion. Loop quantum gravity, string theory,
asymptotic safety, and causal dynamical triangulations are distinct candidate
programs, each with open questions. The Bekenstein–Hawking entropy
$S_{\rm BH}=k_BA/4\ell_P^2$ is a key target for any microscopic theory. In loop
quantum gravity the singularity resolves into a bounce, connecting to
[[White Holes]]. Proposed Lorentz-violating photon dispersion,
$E^2\simeq p^2c^2[1+\eta(E/E_{QG})^n]$, is constrained by GRB 090510
($E_{QG,1}/E_P>1.19$) and by GW170817/GRB 170817A. Wormhole exotic matter in
[[Wormholes]] also motivates quantum-gravity effects.

See also: [[Hawking Radiation]], [[White Holes]], [[Gravitational Wave Analysis]], [[Wormholes]]

Categories: Quantum Gravity

nodes.name: Raychaudhuri Equation
nodes.summary: The Raychaudhuri equation describes how a congruence of geodesics expands, shears, and rotates. It is the geometric heart of the focusing theorem and the singularity theorems.

knowledgeMeta.content:
# Raychaudhuri Equation

The Raychaudhuri equation describes how a congruence of geodesics expands,
shears, and rotates. It is the geometric heart of the focusing theorem and the
singularity theorems.

## Kinematics

For a timelike congruence with $u^\mu u_\mu=-1$ and projection tensor
$h_{\mu\nu}=g_{\mu\nu}+u_\mu u_\nu$, the derivative decomposes as

$$\nabla_\nu u_\mu = \frac13\theta h_{\mu\nu}+\sigma_{\mu\nu}+\omega_{\mu\nu}-u_\mu a_\nu,$$

where $\theta=\nabla_\mu u^\mu$ is the expansion, $\sigma_{\mu\nu}$ the shear,
$\omega_{\mu\nu}$ the vorticity, and $a_\mu$ the acceleration (zero for
geodesics). The null case uses a 2-screen projection with an auxiliary null
vector $\ell^\mu$ satisfying $k^\mu\ell_\mu=-1$.

## The equations

For a timelike geodesic congruence,

$$\frac{d\theta}{d\tau} = -\frac13\theta^2-\sigma_{\mu\nu}\sigma^{\mu\nu}+\omega_{\mu\nu}\omega^{\mu\nu}-R_{\mu\nu}u^\mu u^\nu,$$

and for an affinely parametrized null congruence,

$$\frac{d\theta}{d\lambda} = -\frac12\theta^2-\sigma_{\mu\nu}\sigma^{\mu\nu}+\omega_{\mu\nu}\omega^{\mu\nu}-R_{\mu\nu}k^\mu k^\nu.$$

Expansion and shear focus the congruence; vorticity defocuses it. If the
congruence is hypersurface-orthogonal ($\omega=0$), vorticity stays zero.

## Focusing and singularity theorems

With the strong energy condition ($R_{\mu\nu}u^\mu u^\nu\ge0$) or the null
energy condition ($R_{\mu\nu}k^\mu k^\nu\ge0$), initially converging congruences
focus to a caustic in finite affine parameter. This underlies the Penrose,
Hawking, and Hawking–Penrose singularity theorems and Hawking's area theorem.
It also governs gravitational lensing, where $d\ln A/d\lambda=\theta$, and
black-hole thermodynamics, where equilibrium requires $\theta=0$. The
equations are built from [[Christoffel Symbols]] and the [[Geodesic Equations]],
and they connect to the NEC-violating matter of [[White Holes]] and to
accretion flows in [[Black Hole Accretion]].

See also: [[Geodesic Equations]], [[Christoffel Symbols]], [[White Holes]], [[Black Hole Accretion]]

Categories: Gravity & Spacetime

nodes.name: Reissner-Nordström Metric
nodes.summary: The Reissner–Nordström solution describes a static, spherically symmetric black hole with mass $M$ and electric charge $Q$. It is the charged generalization of the Schwarzschild metric.

knowledgeMeta.content:
# Reissner-Nordström Metric

The Reissner–Nordström solution describes a static, spherically symmetric black
hole with mass $M$ and electric charge $Q$. It is the charged generalization of
the Schwarzschild metric.

## Einstein–Maxwell solution

Starting from the Einstein–Maxwell action and a static, spherically symmetric
ansatz $ds^2=-f(r)dt^2+f(r)^{-1}dr^2+r^2 d\Omega^2$ with $A_t=-Q/r$, the field
equations give

$$f(r) = 1 - \frac{2GM}{r} + \frac{GQ^2}{r^2}.$$

The horizons are the roots of $f(r)=0$:

$$r_\pm = GM \pm \sqrt{G^2M^2 - GQ^2},$$

with $r_+$ the event horizon and $r_-$ the Cauchy horizon. The three regimes are
subextremal ($GM^2>Q^2$), extremal ($GM^2=Q^2$, $r_+=r_-=GM$), and
superextremal ($GM^2<Q^2$, a naked singularity forbidden by cosmic censorship).
At extremality the near-horizon geometry is $AdS_2\times S^2$.

## Thermodynamics

The surface gravity and Hawking temperature are

$$\kappa = \frac{r_+-r_-}{2r_+^2}, \qquad
T_H = \frac{r_+-r_-}{4\pi r_+^2},$$

and the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy is $S=\pi r_+^2/G$. The first law and Smarr
formula are

$$dM = \frac{\kappa}{8\pi G}dA + \Phi_+ dQ, \qquad
M = 2T_H S + \Phi_+ Q,$$

with $\Phi_+=Q/r_+$. The heat capacity $C_Q$ diverges at $r_+^2=3GQ^2$
(Davies phase transition). A charged hole can also discharge by Schwinger pair
production, $dQ/dt \sim -(e^3Q/\pi^2 r_+^2)\exp(-\pi m_e^2 r_+^2/eQ)$.

## Rotating and charged black holes

Adding rotation yields [[Kerr-Newman Metric]]; the uncharged, non-rotating limit
is [[Schwarzschild Metric]]. Horizon structure and quantum emission connect to
[[Hawking Radiation]], and the connection components used in dynamics are in
[[Christoffel Symbols]].

See also: [[Kerr-Newman Metric]], [[Schwarzschild Metric]], [[Hawking Radiation]], [[Christoffel Symbols]]

Categories: Black Holes, Gravity & Spacetime

knowledgeMeta.content:
# Schwarzschild Metric

The Schwarzschild metric is the unique spherically symmetric vacuum solution of
Einstein's field equations (Birkhoff's theorem). It describes the exterior
spacetime of any non-rotating, uncharged mass and is the simplest black-hole
geometry.

## Metric and horizon

The most general static, spherically symmetric line element can be written
$ds^2 = -e^{2\alpha(r)}c^2 dt^2 + e^{2\beta(r)}dr^2 + r^2 d\Omega^2$. Imposing
$R_{\mu\nu}=0$ and asymptotic flatness gives $\alpha = -\beta$ and

$$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \frac{2GM}{rc^2}\right)c^2 dt^2 + \left(1 - \frac{2GM}{rc^2}\right)^{-1}dr^2 + r^2 d\Omega^2$$

with Schwarzschild radius

$$R_s = \frac{2GM}{c^2}.$$

For the Sun, $R_s \approx 2.95$ km.

## Singularity and curvature

At $r=R_s$ the metric is degenerate, but this is a coordinate singularity: the
Kretschmann scalar

$$K = R_{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}R^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma} = \frac{48 G^2 M^2}{c^4 r^6}$$

is finite there. At $r=0$, $K\to\infty$, which is a true curvature singularity.
Kruskal–Szekeres coordinates remove the horizon coordinate singularity and
reveal four regions, including the black-hole interior and the white-hole
region of [[White Holes]].

## Orbits and key radii

Conserved energy $E=(1-R_s/r)c^2 \dot t$ and angular momentum $L=r^2\dot\phi$
give the effective potential

$$V_{\rm eff}(r) = c^2\left(1-\frac{R_s}{r}\right)\left(1+\frac{L^2}{c^2 r^2}\right).$$

Circular photon orbits (the photon sphere) sit at $r_{\rm ph}=3GM/c^2=1.5R_s$,
and the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) at $r_{\rm ISCO}=6GM/c^2=3R_s$.
Tidal acceleration across a body of size $\ell$ is
$a_{\rm tidal}=2GM\ell/r^3$, which for a solar-mass hole at the horizon is
$\sim 2\times10^8 g$.

## Where to go next

The charged generalization is [[Reissner-Nordström Metric]]; adding rotation
gives [[Kerr Metric]] and, with both, [[Kerr-Newman Metric]]. Orbital motion is
treated in [[Geodesic Equations]], and quantum emission in
[[Hawking Radiation]].

See also: [[Kerr Metric]], [[Geodesic Equations]], [[Hawking Radiation]],
[[White Holes]], [[Gravitational Wave Analysis]]

knowledgeMeta.content:
# White Holes

A white hole is the time-reversed Schwarzschild solution: a region of spacetime
from which matter and light can only emerge. It appears as region IV of the
maximal Kruskal–Szekeres extension.

## Geometry

Under $t\to-t$ the Schwarzschild metric is invariant, but the causal structure
differs. In Kruskal coordinates $U,V$ the four regions are: (I) exterior,
(II) black-hole interior, (III) parallel exterior, (IV) white-hole interior.
Region IV has a past singularity at $r=0$ and $r$ increases toward the future,
so nothing can enter from region I. The horizon $r=r_s$ is a null surface with
surface gravity $\kappa=c^4/(4GM)=c^2/(2r_s)$.

## Instability

White holes are catastrophically unstable. Perturbations obey the
Regge–Wheeler equation with reversed boundary conditions, and the instability
e-folding time is $\tau\sim 2r_s/c=4GM/c^3$, comparable to the free-fall time.
Mass inflation drives the interior mass to diverge on the same timescale. For a
solar-mass hole this is $\sim10^{-5}$ s; for a $10^9M_\odot$ hole, a few hours.

## Can they exist?

Classically, white holes are forbidden by the second law and by cosmic
censorship, and no known formation mechanism exists. Quantum mechanically, the
tunneling amplitude $\mathcal A\sim e^{-4\pi GM^2/\hbar c}$ is exponentially
suppressed for macroscopic masses. In loop quantum gravity the singularity
resolves into a quantum bounce and a black hole can transition to a white hole
(a "Planck star"), with bounce time $\sim(M/m_P)^{4/3}t_P$.

## Observational signatures and limits

Speculative signatures include white-hole explosions powering gamma-ray bursts
and fast radio bursts, with luminosity $L\sim c^5/(2G)\sim10^{52}$ W independent
of mass. CMB spectral distortions place an extremely tight limit on any
present-day population, $\rho_{\rm WH}\lesssim10^{-53}$ m$^{-3}$.

See also: [[Schwarzschild Metric]], [[Wormholes]], [[Hawking Radiation]], [[Quantum Gravity]], [[Gravitational Wave Analysis]]

Categories: White Holes, Gravity & Spacetime

knowledgeMeta.content:
# Wormholes

A wormhole is a topological shortcut connecting two regions of spacetime. The
modern theory of traversable wormholes begins with Morris and Thorne (1988),
and it shows that such objects require exotic matter violating the null energy
condition (NEC).

## Morris–Thorne metric

The general static, spherically symmetric traversable metric is

$$ds^2 = -e^{2\Phi(r)}c^2 dt^2 + \frac{dr^2}{1-b(r)/r} + r^2 d\Omega^2,$$

where $\Phi(r)$ is the redshift function and $b(r)$ the shape function. The
throat is the minimum of the areal radius, where $b(r_0)=r_0$. Asymptotic
flatness requires $\Phi\to0$ and $b/r\to0$ as $r\to\infty$.

## Flare-out and exotic matter

Embedding the equatorial slice in $\mathbb R^3$ gives
$dz/dr=\pm\sqrt{r/b(r)-1}$, and the throat must flare outward:

$$\frac{d^2 r}{dz^2}>0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad b'(r_0)<1.$$

The Einstein equations give an anisotropic fluid with
$\rho c^2 = (c^4/8\pi G)\,b'/r^2$. At the throat with $\Phi(r_0)=0$,

$$\rho c^2 + p_r\big|_{r_0} = \frac{c^4}{8\pi G}\frac{b'(r_0)-1}{r_0^2}<0,$$

so the NEC is violated and all stronger energy conditions fail. The violation
is enormous: for $r_0=1$ m and $b'(r_0)=0$, $|\rho c^2+p_r|\approx4.8\times10^{42}$ J/m$^3$.

## Traversability, thin shells, and time travel

Traversability requires no horizon ($\Phi$ finite) and tolerable tidal forces.
Visser's thin-shell construction concentrates the exotic matter on a
codimension-1 shell, minimizing the total amount. Quantum inequalities
constrain how long exotic matter can persist, suggesting Planck-scale throats
for known fields. A moving mouth can produce closed timelike curves, but
Hawking's chronology protection conjecture argues that vacuum polarization
destroys the wormhole first.

## Observational signatures

Wormholes differ from black holes ([[Schwarzschild Metric]]) in shadow size,
lensing (roughly half the Schwarzschild deflection), absence of an event
horizon, and gravitational-wave echoes. Echoes connect to
[[Gravitational Wave Analysis]], and the exotic-matter requirement connects to
[[Quantum Gravity]]. A wormhole is not a white hole ([[White Holes]]), though
both are time-related curiosities.

See also: [[Schwarzschild Metric]], [[White Holes]], [[Raychaudhuri Equation]], [[Gravitational Wave Analysis]], [[Quantum Gravity]]

nodes.name: Karl Schwarzschild
nodes.summary: Discoverer of the Schwarzschild metric, the unique spherically symmetric vacuum solution referenced throughout the wiki.

nodes.name: Roy Kerr
nodes.summary: Discoverer of the Kerr metric, the unique stationary axisymmetric rotating black hole solution.

nodes.name: BlackCAT
nodes.summary: Published catalog compiling black-hole X-ray binaries used to trace stellar-mass black holes via accretion.

nodes.name: GWOSC
nodes.summary: The Gravitational Wave Open Science Center, which serves the GWTC catalog JSON endpoint used by the workspace snapshot.

nodes.name: GW150914
nodes.summary: First gravitational-wave detection (m1 = 36, m2 = 29 solar masses), the anchor example of the remnant sample.

nodes.name: Bardeen–Press–Teukolsky ISCO
nodes.summary: The exact Kerr ISCO formula cited in the Kerr Metric page.

nodes.name: ISCO efficiency sets the luminosity budget
nodes.summary: Up to ~5.7% of rest mass is radiated at the Schwarzschild ISCO and up to ~42% for prograde orbits at the extremal Kerr ISCO — the efficiency bound connecting accretion luminosity to growth.

nodes.name: A stellar-mass black hole is colder than the CMB
nodes.summary: A solar-mass black hole has T_H ~ 6e-8 K, far colder than the CMB (~2.7 K), so it currently absorbs more radiation than it emits.

nodes.name: Solar-mass evaporation time is ~2e67 years
nodes.summary: Neglecting greybody factors, a solar-mass black hole survives ~2e67 years, so evaporation matters only for microscopic remnants.

nodes.name: Ringdown tests the Kerr hypothesis
nodes.summary: The no-hair theorem fixes the quasinormal ringdown spectrum by mass M and spin J alone, so measuring multiple ringdown modes tests whether astrophysical black holes are Kerr.

nodes.name: High-SNR posteriors are Gaussian via the Fisher matrix
nodes.summary: In the high signal-to-noise limit the parameter posterior is approximately multivariate Gaussian with covariance equal to the inverse Fisher matrix.

nodes.name: Eddington-limited e-folding time is ~50 Myr
nodes.summary: For radiative efficiency 0.1 and continuous Eddington-limited accretion the mass e-folding time is about 50 Myr, setting the growth budget for early SMBH seeds.

nodes.name: A GW catalog is not a population census
nodes.summary: GWTC records detected (selected) merger events; it is not a complete or population-unbiased census, and missing parameters must not be read as zero.

nodes.name: Workspace snapshot carries 391 GWTC events
nodes.summary: The local GWOSC snapshot holds a deduplicated 391-event GWTC table plus a 301-event O4 table.

nodes.name: Stephen Hawking
nodes.summary: Predicted Hawking radiation; jointly responsible (with Penrose) for the singularity theorems referenced by the Raychaudhuri page.

nodes.name: Roger Penrose
nodes.summary: Proved the relativistic singularity theorems that build on the Raychaudhuri focusing result.

nodes.name: Morris & Thorne (1988)
nodes.summary: The 1988 paper establishing the modern theory of traversable wormholes and the exotic-matter requirement.

nodes.name: Kruskal–Szekeres extension
nodes.summary: The maximal extension of the Schwarzschild geometry exposing four regions, including the white-hole interior.

nodes.name: Regge–Wheeler equation
nodes.summary: Perturbation equation governing radiative instabilities of the Schwarzschild geometry, used with reversed boundary conditions for white holes.

nodes.name: GWTC
nodes.summary: The Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog of compact-binary merger events published by LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA through GWOSC.

nodes.name: Superextremal charged black holes are naked singularities
nodes.summary: For GM^2 < Q^2 no horizon remains and the singularity is naked, forbidden by cosmic censorship; only subextremal or extremal RN black holes are physical.

nodes.name: Extremal RN near-horizon geometry is AdS2×S2
nodes.summary: At extremality (GM^2 = Q^2, r+ = r- = GM) the near-horizon region becomes AdS2×S2.

nodes.name: Traversable wormholes require exotic matter
nodes.summary: The Morris–Thorne flare-out analysis shows a traversable throat requires violation of the null energy condition, i.e. exotic matter.

nodes.name: White holes are catastrophically unstable
nodes.summary: Perturbations obey the Regge–Wheeler equation with reversed boundary conditions; the instability e-folding time is comparable to the free-fall time (~4GM/c^3).

nodes.name: Astrophysical black holes are expected to be approximately Kerr
nodes.summary: As the unique stationary axisymmetric vacuum solution, Kerr is the expected geometry of real rotating black holes.

nodes.name: No complete quantum gravity is experimentally confirmed
nodes.summary: Matter QFT on curved backgrounds is predictive and yields Hawking radiation, but a complete quantum theory of spacetime remains unconfirmed at the Planck scale.
